MCD.rationale: McDonald's is a high-quality franchise with best-in-class operating margins (~45-46%), a 95% franchised model generating stable royalty/rent income, and a strong brand moat. Q1 2026 showed solid YoY growth (revenue +9%, EPS +7% to $2.78, global comps +3.8%) and the company beat consensus estimates. However, several headwinds temper enthusiasm: (1) QoQ trajectory is negative — revenue -7.9%, EPS -12.6% from Q3 2025 levels, reflecting sequential deceleration; (2) the stock has declined ~17% over the past quarter to $275, near its 52-week low of $272, suggesting the market has already priced in weakness; (3) management explicitly warned Q2 comps will decelerate 'meaningfully' due to tough Minecraft movie tie-in comparisons; (4) U.S. company-operated margins are 'not acceptable' per CFO, with refranchising review underway; (5) rising oil prices ($105/bbl) and consumer softness, especially among low-income consumers, pose ongoing risk; (6) negative equity (-$1.29B) reflects aggressive capital returns via buybacks/dividends funded by debt. The valuation data is unfortunately broken (PE=0 across all history), making Pillar 2 assessment imprecise, but the stock near 52-week lows with a ~2.2% dividend yield and ~3.4% total shareholder yield suggests moderate value. No clear near-term fundamental catalyst exists — the next event is September's Investor Day. Net: solid franchise at a reasonable but not compelling entry point, with near-term earnings trajectory softening.
